releases.name: v0.1.12: learn: passkeys, keys, GCP, and the passkey lab
releases.notes: A learn section, from Dinis's reading of the security page: the words link to explanations in this site's context. Passkeys, WebAuthn and PRF (what the passkey is here and is not; the two calls drawn; what the authenticator, the browser, this site and Google each hold; the RP ID; what two passkeys mean), Keys (is there a passphrase, no; the PRF salt, HKDF, the wrapping keys, the KEK, AES-256-GCM, the recovery code; what is in memory when), and GCP from this site's side (Identity Platform, the uid, the bucket, the Security Rules, Terraform, Workload Identity Federation; what Google sees and cannot). A glossary in data/terms.json, linked by the build from the first use of each term on every content page with the definition as hover text, and listed by the reader's column under a Terms tab. Flow diagrams drawn by the build from data/diagrams/ as inline SVG on the theme's tokens, with the same diagram as text. The passkey lab on the passkeys page: create lab passkeys in your own browser under this host's RP ID, ask for the PRF bytes (same salt, same bytes; another salt, others), derive the wrapping key, wrap a lab KEK, encrypt a lab body, forget the keys, unlock again with the same or a second passkey, and watch what is stored where; one allow-listed storage record of public values, no network. Chromium's virtual authenticator does PRF, which answers an open question of the brief (C25). Twins keep explicit anchors as inline HTML so fragment links into them resolve.

releases.name: v0.1.11: code mode
releases.notes: The navigator has two modes. Intent is the brief downwards, as before, with the claims folded by status and release and the left column foldable. Code is entered by opening a file, picking the Code view, or the switch in the top bar: the source in the middle with the selected lines marked, the file's tree on the left (packages, files, classes, methods), and on the right the graph upwards from that piece of code: what it says about itself (its own comments), why it exists (the claims whose evidence lives in it and the stories they realise), outline, imports and importers, calls and callers, tests and surfaces. The derived layers under review/graph/ (files, modules, classes, methods, tests, surfaces, and an index of counts and paths) come from review/tools/derive.py: Python through ast, JavaScript through a vendored, hashed acorn that only the build runs. Every file path a node names is a link into the source. The explanation layer (what, why, story, at a technical and a business level) is proposed in C24.

releases.name: v0.1.9: everything links to everything
releases.notes: Meaning through connectivity, from the fractal semantic graphs article: a claim means nothing until it is linked to its evidence, down to an anchor a person can open. Every claim in data/features.json now carries typed evidence (realises an intent node, lives_in a file, proven_by a test or a gate check, described_in a section or a document, seen_at a URL); review/tools/claims.py turns the claims, the releases (with their commit, tag and Actions run, backfilled from GitHub) and the anchors into the claims layer of the review graph, strict: a shipped claim with no anchor that resolves fails the build. Every status chip and every location on /shipped/ and in the status lines is a link into the navigator. The reader never leaves it to follow a chain: the brief is split into fourteen section files under review/brief/ by review/tools/brief.py and shown in place by review-brief, with the intent nodes written from each section; any served file is shown in place with line numbers and a marked range by review-source; sections and files are routes the gate resolves. The ladder gains the brief and the evidence rungs; the tree gains the Claims and The brief views; the crumb follows. C23, R10.

verified.by: verify-live in the run above, and admin/build/verify_live.py after the push

releases.name: v0.1.8: the prototype: three UX variants and the column
releases.notes: The mockups are now a working prototype on invented data this browser keeps (components/proto-base, the store under sgit.secrets.proto.v1): sign in, create the keyring and the recovery code, add, open, reveal, copy, edit and delete entries, lock and unlock, devices, environment, account, the admin checklist, the probe matrix, routed by the app's own rules. Three UX variants in every frame for A/B testing (A Desk, the brief's shape; B Focus, one card per screen with a tab bar; C Command, a command bar, a dense table and an inspector), the pick kept under sgit.secrets.ui.proto. A column beside every frame (components/proto-column): what the screen is and the intent it realises, the paths to it and from it as a clickable graph, the data as charts (entries by kind, screens visited, actions over the last hour), the last actions, an A/B/C vote that is also a note in the reader's log, and the state as JSON with Seed, Reset and Copy. mockups/screens.json holds the screens, the paths and the variants; /mockups/prototype.html is the whole thing in one frame. The five categorical colours of every theme are now validated hues (C22).

releases.notes: Six content pages: how it works, security, keyring format v1, sharing, environments, and /shipped/ generated from data/features.json with one table per status. Every content page opens with a status line generated from the same file. Every markdown document under docs/ is now rendered to an HTML page beside it (the design documents, the ops notes, reality.md) by a standard-library markdown renderer, with index pages for docs/design/ and docs/ops/; the markdown stays the source and the twin. The homepage links the new pages and carries the three-step demo as proposed. The chrome now has the family nav (grouped menus with dropdowns, the part-of-sgit.ai link, the stage pill, a phone menu) with breadcrumbs, and the admin section gains a comms page with the asks and a tracker of the nine build steps. Versions now bump the third digit per release (brief-corrections C15). v0.1.0 went live at secrets.sgit.ai (DNS, Pages and the re-run done by Dinis), so the live-domain claim is shipped; needs.md items 1 to 3 are closed.
